hero.headline: U.S. and Iran near agreement to end hostilities and reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have escalated military actions in the Strait of Hormuz, raising serious questions about whether ongoing peace negotiations will move forward. The standoff threatens to derail efforts to reopen one of the world's most critical shipping routes.

Iranian naval forces seized two commercial vessels in the strait on Wednesday, accusing them of attempting to exit the waterway covertly. The Panama-flagged MSC Francesca and Liberia-flagged Epaminondas were brought to shore by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The seizures mark the first time Iran has taken control of ships since the conflict began on February 28. These actions came after the U.S. previously fired on and seized an Iranian cargo vessel and boarded an Iranian oil tanker in the Indian Ocean.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Iranian parliament and lead negotiator, said reopening the strait would be "impossible" while what he described as U.S. and Israeli breaches of the ceasefire continue. He criticized the U.S. naval blockade as "the hostage-taking of the world's economy" and warned that military aggression and bullying would not succeed.

The Strait of Hormuz carries approximately 20 percent of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas. Its closure has created a spiraling global economic crisis. About 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships have been stranded in the region, according to the International Maritime Organization.

The White House press secretary said President Trump was "satisfied" with the naval blockade and believes Iran is in a weak position. She stated the U.S. was "completely strangling their economy through this blockade, they're losing $500 million a day." This represents a shift from earlier statements suggesting a deal was near.

Peace talks scheduled to take place in Islamabad failed to materialize. Pakistan had prepared a luxury hotel for negotiations, and a U.S. delegation led by Vice President JD Vance was expected to attend. However, Iranian officials never publicly accepted the invitation, and the American delegation never left Washington.

The economic impact extends globally. Germany, Europe's largest economy, halved its 2026 growth forecast to 0.5 percent. Greece announced 500 million euros in additional aid for households and farmers facing higher fuel and food costs. Countries throughout Asia dependent on Gulf oil have been severely affected, experiencing shortages of fuel, fertilizer, and other raw materials.

The standoff reflects deeper disagreements between the nations. Trump previously withdrew from an agreement limiting Iran's nuclear enrichment program, and Israeli pressure continues to influence U.S. policy. A separate Israeli-Hezbollah conflict in Lebanon, with a fragile ceasefire expiring soon, adds to regional tensions.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes, threatening NASA moon mission timeline
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday evening, creating a massive fireball visible across the state and raising serious questions about NASA's lunar ambitions.

The explosion occurred at 9pm ET during a scheduled hotfire test at Launch Complex 36. The blast destroyed the launchpad and was visible from Fort Pierce, roughly 115 miles to the south. Shockwaves were felt along Florida's space coast, with residents reporting shaking homes in Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach. The incident occurred just one day after NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned uncrewed lunar missions this year to support construction of a $20 billion moon base.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed that all employees were safe and unharmed. He described it as a "very rough day" and said the company was already investigating the cause, which Blue Origin called an "anomaly." Bezos pledged that his company would "rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying."

The New Glenn rocket was specifically designed to launch moon landers for NASA's Artemis program. The rocket is crucial to Blue Origin's planned role in the program, which includes conducting uncrewed lunar landings and competing with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for the Artemis IV mission scheduled for 2028. That mission will mark the first crewed moon landing since 1972.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman acknowledged the severity of the situation, noting that spaceflight is "unforgiving" and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is "extraordinarily difficult." He stated that NASA would conduct a full evaluation of impacts to the Artemis timeline and moon base program following a thorough investigation.

The explosion represents the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin. The company recently experienced a payload deployment failure during a New Glenn flight that placed cargo in the wrong orbit. That incident resulted in a temporary FAA grounding, and Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the agency cleared the rocket to return to flight the previous week.

The incident also highlights the competitive pressure Blue Origin faces from SpaceX in securing NASA contracts. SpaceX founder Elon Musk quickly responded to the explosion on social media, saying "Most unfortunate" and noting that "Rockets are hard."

The FAA did not immediately respond to requests for comment about whether the explosion would trigger a new investigation. Both Blue Origin and SpaceX have built major facilities near Cape Canaveral to support their partnership with NASA on the Artemis program.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Allows Companies to Avoid Billions in Taxes Through Foreign Havens
cards.body:
The Trump administration has cleared the way for U.S. companies to bypass at least $40 billion in taxes since early 2025 through schemes operating in countries including Malta, Bermuda, and Cyprus.

The tax avoidance strategies allow corporations to shift profits to jurisdictions with minimal or no corporate tax rates. Malta and Cyprus, both members of the European Union, have faced scrutiny for offering tax arrangements that critics say enable profit shifting. Bermuda has long served as a haven for companies seeking to reduce their tax obligations.

The $40 billion figure represents taxes companies have skirted since the beginning of 2025. The exact mechanisms enabling this avoidance and which specific policy changes facilitated it remain tied to decisions made under the current administration.

Corporate tax avoidance through offshore jurisdictions has been a persistent issue for decades, with multinational companies using complex structures to legally minimize their tax bills. These arrangements typically involve establishing subsidiaries or intellectual property holdings in low-tax countries, then routing profits through those entities.

The revelation comes as debates over corporate taxation continue in Washington. Previous administrations have attempted various reforms to limit profit shifting, including minimum tax provisions and restrictions on certain offshore structures. The current approach appears to have reversed or relaxed some of those constraints.

Malta and Cyprus have become particularly popular destinations for such arrangements within the European Union framework. Both countries offer favorable tax rulings and structures that allow companies to significantly reduce their effective tax rates while maintaining a presence in an EU member state.

Bermuda has been a traditional favorite for U.S. companies seeking offshore tax benefits, offering a zero percent corporate income tax rate. The island nation hosts thousands of corporate subsidiaries despite its small size and population.

The $40 billion in avoided taxes represents revenue that would otherwise have flowed to the U.S. Treasury. Tax policy experts have long debated the balance between maintaining competitive corporate tax rates and ensuring companies pay their share of government revenues.

cards.headline: Trump administration cuts funding for US infectious disease research centers in Africa
cards.teaser: Infectious disease research centers established during the COVID pandemic have lost federal funding under the current administration.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed at least 240 people since early in the month, with cases spreading to other regions and Uganda's capital. The virus is difficult to contain in Ituri province, a mining hub where thousands work in close proximity and conflict between rebel groups has displaced people into overcrowded camps.

The Trump administration has eliminated funding for US research centers in Africa that were established to strengthen infectious disease surveillance and response. These centers would typically deploy researchers to help combat outbreaks like the current Ebola crisis, but the cuts have sidelined these teams from conducting field work to study and contain disease spread in African countries.

cards.headline: Surface Transportation Board Delays Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern Merger Review
cards.teaser: Federal regulators accepted a revised merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but paused proceedings on the railroad deal.
cards.body:
The Surface Transportation Board accepted a revised merger application from Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern but announced delays in the review proceedings. The merger, valued at between $71.5 billion and $85 billion depending on the source, would create the first transcontinental railroad spanning coast to coast.

The pause in the review process represents a setback for the two major freight rail companies seeking to combine operations. The merger would join Union Pacific's western rail network with Norfolk Southern's eastern routes, fundamentally reshaping American freight transportation. The Surface Transportation Board has regulatory authority over railroad mergers and must approve any deal before it can proceed.

cards.headline: European Union to Release Billions to Hungary After Orban's Defeat
cards.teaser: The EU is set to release 16 billion euros it had withheld as Hungary moves to enact anti-corruption and rule of law policies.
cards.body:
The European Union will release over 16 billion euros to Hungary that had been frozen under Viktor Orbán's rule. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the decision as reflecting "winds of change" following the election of new Prime Minister Péter Magyar last month. Magyar called it a "historic breakthrough" for the country.

The thaw in EU-Hungary relations is accompanied by other policy shifts. Hungarian police announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest to proceed, reversing the previous government's attempt to block the event last year.

hero.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Apartment Building in Romania
hero.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in the Romanian city of Galati on Friday, injuring two people during an overnight attack on neighboring Ukraine. The incident marked the first time a drone strike has caused casualties in Romania, a NATO member state.

The drone struck the roof of the residential building, igniting a fire and forcing evacuations. Romanian authorities tracked the aircraft on radar as it moved through Romanian airspace before impact. Emergency services responded to the scene, and police investigated the incident.

Romania's military responded by scrambling two F-16 fighter jets and a helicopter authorized to engage targets. The government issued emergency alerts to residents in affected areas.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte issued a swift response, stating the alliance is "ready to defend every inch" of its territory. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Rutte wrote on social media after speaking with Romanian President Nicusor Dan. NATO condemned what it characterized as Russia's dangerous escalation.

Russia denied involvement, calling reports of a Russian drone strike "groundless."

Romanian officials convened an emergency meeting of the country's supreme council of national defense and summoned Russia's ambassador. Foreign Minister Oana Toiu announced that Romania would formally communicate the consequences for diplomatic relations and discuss next steps regarding European sanctions against Russia. She described the incident as a "grave and irresponsible escalation" and a serious violation of international law.

Romania's defense ministry stated the strike was not "an attack from Russia against Romania," but emphasized that Russians represent a security threat to countries in the region. President Dan said Romania would not tolerate the Ukrainian conflict spilling into its territory and instructed the foreign ministry to prepare a package of measures regarding relations with Moscow.

Romania requested that NATO accelerate the transfer of anti-drone capabilities and indicated it would invoke Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which triggers formal discussions about threats to member security.

International leaders condemned the strike. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia's "war of aggression has crossed yet another line" and pledged solidarity with Romania. France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot called it an "irresponsible act by Russia" against a European Union and NATO country.

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha characterized the incident as evidence that Russian aggression threatens all of Europe, not just Ukraine. He warned of the broader regional security implications.

The incident follows months of drone incursions into Romanian airspace, though this was the first resulting in civilian injuries. The strike represents a significant escalation of the conflict's spillover effects beyond Ukraine's borders and heightened tensions between Russia and the Western security alliance.

cards.headline: Trump Says He Will Soon Decide on Iran Proposal
cards.teaser: The president said Iran must agree to his demanded concessions and that he was ready to lift the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
President Trump said on social media that he will soon make a final determination on an Iran proposal, adding that Iran must agree to concessions he has demanded. He said he was poised to lift the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran has not confirmed any commitments, according to reports. The Strait of Hormuz is a key waterway for global oil shipments, and the US naval blockade has been in place as part of ongoing tensions between the two countries.

cards.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty to Aiding Suicides by Selling Toxic Substance Online
cards.teaser: A Canadian man admitted to sending suicide packets to hundreds of people around the world.
cards.body:
A Canadian man has pleaded guilty to aiding suicides by selling a toxic chemical online. He admitted to sending suicide packets to hundreds of people worldwide, including recipients in Britain.

Families of victims have questioned how he was able to facilitate so many deaths and have called for him to face charges in the UK. However, he will not be prosecuted under British law.

cards.headline: One Gold Miner Rescued From Flooded Cave in Laos After More Than a Week
cards.teaser: An international rescue effort freed one of five men trapped in a flooded cave, bringing attention to the country's informal mining operations.
cards.body:
Rescuers have successfully extracted the first of seven men trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for over a week. The group had entered the remote cave in Xaysomboun province to hunt wildlife and pan for gold before heavy rains blocked the entrance. The rescued man is now safe, though four others remain inside a chamber about 300 meters from the cave entrance, huddled together on a rocky ledge.

An international team of divers has been deployed to continue the rescue operation, navigating treacherous conditions through narrow, water-filled tunnels. Some team members previously participated in the 2018 Thai soccer team cave rescue. Two miners are still unaccounted for as rescue efforts continue.

cards.headline: Former Head of China's Shaolin Temple Sentenced to 24 Years for Corruption
cards.teaser: Shi Yongxin, the ex-abbot of the famous kung fu temple, was convicted of embezzlement and bribery.
cards.body:
The former head monk of China's Shaolin Temple was sentenced to 24 years in prison for embezzlement and bribery, state media reported. Shi Yongxin led the famous Buddhist temple known internationally for its association with kung fu martial arts.

The Shaolin Temple, located in central China, has become a major tourist attraction and cultural institution. Shi Yongxin served as abbot of the temple before his conviction on corruption charges.

cards.headline: Trump's Boat Strikes Have Not Reduced Cocaine Flow to US, Experts Say
cards.teaser: Despite attacks on drug trafficking vessels off South America, cocaine remains as available in the US as before the strikes began.
cards.body:
Trump administration boat strikes targeting drug trafficking vessels off the South American coast have failed to curb the flow of cocaine into the United States, according to experts. Researchers say cocaine is as easy to obtain in many parts of the country as it was before the strikes began.

The strikes have resulted in a rising body count off South America. The attacks were intended to disrupt drug smuggling operations, but experts say they have not achieved their stated goal of reducing cocaine availability in the US market.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump administration's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge has temporarily halted work on a fund created by the Trump administration to compensate people it claims were targeted by government prosecution.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Virginia temporarily blocked the Trump administration from transferring money into a $1.8 billion fund designed to compensate those the administration claims were victims of government weaponization. US District Judge Leonie Brinkema issued the order on Friday, preventing the government from taking further action on the fund's creation or operation while legal challenges proceed.

The order bars any irreversible dispersal of funds from the anti-weaponization initiative. The legal challenge was brought by a prosecutor involved in January 6 cases, and the court's freeze remains in effect while arguments in the case continue.

cards.headline: Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testifies to Congress on Epstein files release
cards.teaser: Former U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi appeared before lawmakers to explain the Trump administration's handling of Jeffrey Epstein case documents.
cards.body:
Former U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before Congress in a closed-door interview about the Justice Department's handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein. The testimony occurred about a month after President Trump removed Bondi from her role as attorney general in April.

The hearing focused on the release of Epstein case documents and how they were prepared for public disclosure. Lawmakers examined the department's process for managing and releasing the sensitive materials as part of a broader congressional inquiry into the Epstein case.

cards.headline: Five people killed, 34 injured in Virginia bus crash
cards.teaser: A bus collided with cars in Virginia, resulting in multiple deaths and injuries, state police reported.
cards.body:
Five people died and 34 others were injured in a multi-vehicle crash involving a bus in Virginia, state police confirmed. The collision ranks among the deadliest traffic accidents in the state this year.

State police are investigating what caused the crash. Those injured were taken to local hospitals for treatment.

cards.headline: Three people die in fall from London tower block
cards.teaser: A man, woman, and child were found dead after falling from a residential building in Elephant and Castle.
cards.body:
Three people, including a child, died after falling from a tower block in the Elephant and Castle area of London. Emergency services responded to the scene where a man, woman, and child were pronounced dead.

Authorities have not released details about the circumstances surrounding the incident or the identities of those who died. The building is a residential tower block in south London.

cards.headline: Canadian pleads guilty to aiding suicides by selling toxic chemical online
cards.teaser: A Canadian man admitted to helping people end their lives by selling a toxic substance through the internet.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law pleaded guilty in Ontario, Canada to 14 charges of aiding suicide and sending products internationally while knowing they would likely be used to end lives. He sold toxic substances to people across multiple countries, including the United Kingdom.

Bereaved families whose loved ones died say they feel insulted that Law will not face prosecution in Britain. They have called for him to be charged in the UK as well, highlighting their frustration with the decision not to extradite him. Law awaits sentencing.

cards.headline: Greek national charged with helping alleged Iranian intelligence operatives
cards.teaser: British police charged a Greek citizen with assisting people suspected of working for Iranian intelligence.
cards.body:
The Metropolitan Police charged a Greek national with assisting alleged Iranian intelligence operatives who targeted a UK-based journalist working for Iran International, a media outlet covering Iranian affairs.

The charges relate to actions taken to support those suspected of being Iranian spies in their efforts to target the reporter in the United Kingdom.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Drop as U.S.-Iran Ceasefire Extension Appears Closer
cards.teaser: Oil prices fell as investors reacted to signs that a deal to extend a ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran may be within reach.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell Thursday after reports emerged of a potential breakthrough in U.S.-Iran negotiations. The tentative agreement would extend an existing ceasefire, though it remains subject to approval from the Trump administration.

Markets responded positively to the diplomatic progress, with investors viewing a deal as likely to reduce supply disruptions from the Persian Gulf region. The ceasefire extension could ease concerns about stability in one of the world's most critical oil-producing areas.

cards.headline: Anthropic Valued at $900 Billion, Surpassing OpenAI
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company Anthropic reached a $900 billion valuation, overtaking competitor OpenAI as the most valuable AI firm.
cards.body:
Anthropic has raised $65 billion in Series H funding, bringing its valuation to $965 billion and making it the world's most valuable AI startup. The funding round eclipses competitor OpenAI and positions Anthropic ahead of a highly anticipated initial public offering.

The company's rapid ascent reflects widespread adoption of its Claude chatbot by enterprise customers. This growth accelerated following the release of powerful coding assistants, transforming Anthropic from a smaller player into a dominant force in the artificial intelligence industry.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary Backs Proposal to Put Trump on New $250 Bill
cards.teaser: Treasury Secretary Bessent supported a proposal to create a new $250 bill featuring President Trump, which would require new legislation.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the White House is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait. According to Bessent, the new denomination would celebrate the country's 250th anniversary of independence.

The proposal would break with federal law, which currently prohibits living individuals from appearing on U.S. currency. The Treasury Department has already begun preparing for the possibility of producing the new bill, though congressional approval and a change to existing law would be required. Democrats have indicated they plan to block the measure.

cards.headline: Wall Street Banks Line Up Behind SpaceX Public Offering
cards.teaser: Investment banks are working with Elon Musk to build momentum for the SpaceX initial public offering, aiming to convince investors the opportunity outweighs the risks.
cards.body:
Elon Musk and investment bankers are building support for the SpaceX public offering, attempting to create momentum that makes investors feel passing up the deal carries more risk than buying into it. The effort represents a coordinated push to ensure strong demand for what would be one of the largest IPOs in history.

The strategy involves generating hype around the space company's prospects while Wall Street firms position themselves to profit from the deal. SpaceX has become one of the most closely watched private companies, with its valuation and plans for going public drawing intense scrutiny from investors and analysts.

cards.headline: Ferrari Faces Backlash Over Electric Vehicle Design
cards.teaser: Ferrari's first electric car encountered criticism in Italy and internationally, with reactions calling it the company's most divisive vehicle.
cards.body:
Ferrari's debut electric vehicle, the Luce model, has sparked widespread criticism over its design. The car has divided opinion on social media, with sharp backlash emerging in Italy and beyond. The controversy has impacted the company's stock price, with Ferrari shares slumping following the unveiling.

The polarizing reception marks a significant moment for the luxury automaker, which has long maintained an aspirational cultural status. The new model arrives as Ferrari faces mounting pressure from Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers in the competitive EV market.

cards.headline: South Korean chip startup raises $135 million, betting on memory as AI bottleneck
cards.teaser: XCENA secured funding based on its premise that memory, not computing power, limits artificial intelligence performance.
cards.body:
South Korean semiconductor startup XCENA raised $135 million in new funding. The company argues that the primary constraint on AI systems is memory access and bandwidth rather than raw processing capability.

The investment reflects growing industry attention to chip architectures designed specifically for AI workloads. Traditional computing systems often struggle to feed data quickly enough to processors, creating bottlenecks that slow down machine learning tasks regardless of how powerful the chips themselves may be.

cards.headline: China launches new crew to space station with astronaut assigned to yearlong mission
cards.teaser: A fresh crew launched to the Tiangong space station, including one astronaut who will remain in orbit for a full year.
cards.body:
China sent three astronauts to its Tiangong space station aboard the Shenzhou-23 mission, launched Sunday from the Jiuquan launch centre in northwestern China. One crew member will spend a full year in orbit, marking the first time China has conducted such an extended-duration spaceflight.

The yearlong mission is a significant step toward Beijing's goal of landing humans on the moon by 2030. Extended missions in orbit help prepare for the physiological demands and technical requirements of deep space exploration.

cards.headline: Acer releases $699 laptop with Intel chips to compete with MacBook
cards.teaser: Acer introduced the Swift Air 14, a $699 laptop positioned as an alternative to Apple's MacBook lineup.
cards.body:
Acer unveiled the Swift Air 14, a 14-inch laptop starting at $699 designed to compete directly with Apple's MacBook Neo. The device features Intel's Core Series 3 "Wildcat Lake" processors—available in Core 5 or Core 7 configurations, both six-core chips—paired with 8GB of RAM. The laptop is available in green and emphasizes portability and affordability for Windows users.

The launch reflects PC manufacturers' efforts to challenge Apple's latest MacBook offerings. Acer is positioning the Swift Air 14 as a compelling alternative for consumers seeking MacBook-like performance and design at a significantly lower price point.

cards.headline: Intel releases Arc G3 processors targeting handheld gaming devices
cards.teaser: Intel launched its Arc G3 chip family designed specifically for portable gaming PCs.
cards.body:
Intel introduced the Arc G3 series of processors aimed at the handheld gaming PC market. The chips are designed to power portable devices that can run PC games on the go, competing with existing handheld gaming systems.

Multiple manufacturers are adopting the new processors. Acer announced the Predator Atlas 8 handheld powered by Intel chips, while MSI revealed the Claw 8 EX AI Plus gaming handheld. The releases signal Intel's push to establish a presence in the growing portable gaming hardware segment.

cards.headline: Rare tree propagated at botanic gardens after clinging to cliffside habitat
cards.teaser: A tree believed to be the last of its kind in the wild has been successfully cultivated at botanical gardens.
cards.body:
Botanical gardens have grown new specimens from a tree that had been surviving alone on a cliffside. The tree was considered the last remaining individual of its kind in its natural habitat.

The successful propagation offers hope for preserving the species beyond its precarious wild location. Botanical gardens often serve as genetic repositories for endangered plants, maintaining populations that can eventually support reintroduction efforts or provide material for scientific research.

hero.headline: Jose Mourinho returns to Real Madrid as head coach
hero.body:
Jose Mourinho has agreed to a three-year contract to become Real Madrid head coach for the second time. The Portuguese manager previously led the Spanish club from 2010 to 2013.

During his first spell at the Bernabéu, Mourinho won La Liga in 2012, a significant achievement that broke Barcelona's grip on Spanish football. He also won the Copa del Rey in 2011 and the Spanish Super Cup in 2012.

Mourinho's return comes after Real Madrid parted ways with their previous manager following a disappointing season. The club finished outside the top two in La Liga and exited the Champions League in the quarterfinals, falling short of the standards expected at one of European football's biggest institutions.

At 63 years old, Mourinho brings extensive experience from his managerial career across Europe. Since leaving Real Madrid in 2013, he has managed Chelsea for a second spell, Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, and most recently AS Roma. During his career, he has won league titles in Portugal, England, Italy, and Spain. He has also claimed the Champions League twice, first with Porto in 2004 and later with Inter Milan in 2010.

Mourinho's appointment comes as Real Madrid targets a return to dominance in both domestic and European competitions. The club is now named as the most valuable club in world football, according to recent valuations. Barcelona has overtaken Manchester United to claim second place in the financial rankings.

The manager is recognized for his tactical expertise and proven ability to organize effective defensive systems. His track record of winning trophies across multiple clubs makes him a high-profile appointment for the Spanish giants.

As Mourinho prepares for his new role, he will focus on assembling his coaching staff and evaluating the current squad. The upcoming transfer window will offer opportunities to strengthen the team according to his tactical philosophy and vision for the club's future direction.

The three-year deal represents a substantial commitment from both Mourinho and Real Madrid as they seek to restore the club to its winning ways. Real Madrid has historically been one of Europe's most successful clubs, and the appointment of an experienced manager like Mourinho signals the club's determination to compete for major honors in the seasons ahead.

His return to the Bernabéu marks another significant chapter in his managerial career and represents Real Madrid's confidence in his ability to lead the club back to sustained success at the highest levels of Spanish and European football.

cards.headline: Tennis player criticized for saying woman should not have umpired his match
cards.teaser: Adolfo Daniel Vallejo drew criticism after stating his French Open match should not have been umpired by a woman.
cards.body:
Adolfo Daniel Vallejo faced criticism after stating that his French Open second-round match should not have been umpired by a woman.

Tennis has increasingly worked to advance gender equality in officiating, with women now regularly serving as chair umpires at Grand Slam tournaments.

cards.headline: Players call for removal of sponsorship boards after French Open injury
cards.teaser: Katie Boulter and other players are calling for on-court advertising boards to be removed after a player was injured tripping over one.
cards.body:
Britain's Katie Boulter has called for the French Open to remove its on-court sponsorship boards following an injury to Turkey's Zeynep Sonmez, who retired from her match after tripping over one of the advertising boards placed on the playing surface.

The incident has prompted safety concerns among players about the placement of sponsorship materials during the tournament.

cards.headline: Champions League final will require paid subscription to watch
cards.teaser: The Champions League final between Arsenal and PSG will not be available on free television after TNT Sports declined to make it freely accessible.
cards.body:
Fans will need a TNT Sports subscription to watch the Champions League final between Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain. The broadcaster has decided against making the match available on free-to-air television, despite pressure to do so.

This decision means the high-profile match will remain behind a paywall rather than being accessible to a wider audience at no cost.

cards.headline: Real Madrid named most valuable football club
cards.teaser: Real Madrid has been ranked as the most valuable club in world football, with Barcelona moving into second place ahead of Manchester United.
cards.body:
Real Madrid has been named the most valuable club in world football. Barcelona has claimed second place, overtaking Manchester United in the rankings.

This shift represents a significant change in the financial hierarchy of European football, with both Spanish clubs now occupying the top two positions in global club valuations.

cards.headline: New Zealand defeats Ireland by innings and 79 runs in one-off Test
cards.teaser: New Zealand won the one-off Test against Ireland at Stormont by a substantial margin on the third day of play.
cards.body:
New Zealand completed a decisive victory over Ireland in their one-off Test match at Stormont, finishing the contest on the third day. The winning margin of an innings and 79 runs underscored the home side's dominance throughout the match.

Ireland struggled to mount meaningful resistance across both innings, unable to accumulate the runs necessary to compete effectively against New Zealand's strong performance.

cards.headline: Steve Clarke extends Scotland contract after considering departure
cards.teaser: Scotland head coach Steve Clarke signed a new deal after nearly leaving the position, saying he believes he is the best person for the role.
cards.body:
Steve Clarke said he decided to continue as Scotland head coach because he is convinced he is the best person for the job. The manager signed a new deal after coming close to leaving the position.

Clarke's near departure would have marked the end of his tenure leading the national team. His decision to stay represents a reversal after apparently considering his future with the Scottish Football Association.

hero.headline: Filmmaker Jorge Gutierrez Drops Amazon AI Animation Project After Backlash
hero.body:
Filmmaker Jorge Gutierrez announced he will no longer produce an AI-generated animated series for Amazon Prime Video and apologized for his involvement in the project. The decision came after public criticism this week following news that he would participate in Amazon MGM Studios' new initiative to fund AI entertainment projects.

Gutierrez said he apologized to those he upset with his involvement in the AI-generated series. The filmmaker did not provide additional details about the specific nature of the backlash or what prompted his change of direction.

Amazon MGM Studios had recently launched an initiative specifically dedicated to funding AI-generated entertainment projects. The program represented the company's entry into developing content created primarily through artificial intelligence technology.

The announcement of Gutierrez's participation in the AI project drew immediate criticism. Within days of the news breaking, the filmmaker reversed course and withdrew from the production entirely.

Gutierrez is known for his work in animation. His decision to step away from the Amazon project marks a significant reversal in what appeared to be a major streaming platform's push into AI-generated content.

The series would have been part of Amazon Prime Video's streaming lineup. No information was provided about whether Amazon plans to continue with the project using different creators or if the initiative will proceed without Gutierrez's involvement.

The controversy highlights ongoing debates in the entertainment industry about the use of artificial intelligence in content creation. Artists and creators have expressed concerns about AI-generated work potentially displacing human creators and the ethical implications of such technology in filmmaking and animation.

Gutierrez's apology acknowledged the upset caused by his initial decision to participate in the project. His withdrawal represents one of the most visible instances of a creator publicly reversing course on an AI entertainment venture after facing public pressure.

cards.headline: A24's The Backrooms Earns $10.4 Million in Thursday Previews, Breaking Studio Record
cards.teaser: The horror film based on Kane Parsons' YouTube series shattered A24's preview record and is expected to continue strong at theaters.
cards.body:
A24 and Chernin Entertainment's horror film The Backrooms earned $10.4 million in Thursday preview screenings, setting a new record for A24's highest preview earnings. The movie is based on director Kane Parsons' creepy YouTube series of the same name.

The preview performance positions The Backrooms as another potential hit for movie theaters. The film's strong opening night surpassed all previous A24 releases in preview ticket sales, signaling significant audience interest in the YouTube-to-film adaptation.

cards.headline: Emilia Clarke Discusses Game of Thrones Pay, Ponies Season 2, and Survivor's Guilt
cards.teaser: The actress opened up about salary rumors from her HBO series, her current projects, and feelings of having cheated death.
cards.body:
Emilia Clarke reflected on her career trajectory following the 2019 Emmy Awards, when she set a goal to redefine what she viewed as success. At that point, Clarke had already starred in major franchises including Terminator and Star Wars spinoffs, and was widely recognized for her portrayal of a warrior in the premium drama Game of Thrones.

Clarke addressed rumors about her Game of Thrones salary and discussed the upcoming second season of Ponies. She also spoke about experiencing survivor's guilt, describing a feeling that she had cheated death and that death was coming to get her. The interview covered both her professional achievements and personal reflections on mortality.

cards.headline: A Different World Sequel Series to Premiere on Netflix in September
cards.teaser: The new series set at Hillman College will debut 39 years after the original Cosby Show spinoff first aired.
cards.body:
Netflix will premiere a sequel series to A Different World on Sept. 24, exactly 39 years after the original show debuted in 1987. The new series is set at the same fictional historically Black college, Hillman College, that served as the backdrop for the original Cosby Show spinoff.

Maleah Joi Moon leads the cast as Deborah Wayne, the daughter of a character from the original series. The show continues the legacy of the 1987 edition by returning to the same educational setting while following a new generation of students at the HBCU.

cards.headline: Blippi and Meekah to Release Disneyland-Themed Episodes on YouTube
cards.teaser: Two episodes filmed at the Anaheim park will premiere on the Blippi YouTube channel in late May and mid-June.
cards.body:
Blippi and Meekah will premiere two Disneyland-themed episodes filmed at the Disney park in Anaheim, California. The first episode will debut on the Blippi YouTube channel on May 30, with the second following on June 13.

Disney described the Disneyland Resort as full of imagination, adventure and discovery around every corner, positioning it as an ideal setting for the children's entertainment brand. The episodes mark a collaboration between the YouTube channels and the theme park destination.

cards.headline: Riot Fest 2026 Lineup Features Alanis Morissette, Morrissey, and Nas
cards.teaser: The Chicago festival will also host both Sex Pistols featuring Frank Carter and Johnny Rotten's Public Image Ltd.
cards.body:
Riot Fest announced its 2026 lineup with headliners including Alanis Morissette, Morrissey, and Nas. The Chicago event will feature a diverse range of musical acts spanning multiple genres and decades.

The festival will include performances from both Sex Pistols featuring Frank Carter and Johnny Rotten's Public Image Ltd., creating a near-reunion of the influential punk band's members across two separate sets at the same event.

cards.headline: Prime Video's Off Campus Success Leads to American Eagle and Hot Topic Collections
cards.teaser: The romantic drama about hockey has broken streaming records and spawned multiple branded merchandise partnerships.
cards.body:
Prime Video's "Off Campus" has achieved such strong streaming performance that major retailers are launching themed merchandise collections. American Eagle and Hot Topic are among the brands creating products tied to the romantic drama series, which centers on hockey and relationships.

The show's breakout success demonstrates how streaming hits reach a critical threshold where commercial partnerships become inevitable. Brand collaborations like these represent a standard next step for series that capture significant audience attention.

hero.headline: Kenyan court blocks US Ebola quarantine facility
hero.teaser: A court halted government permission for the United States to establish a quarantine facility for Americans exposed to Ebola virus spreading in northeastern Congo.
hero.body:
The Trump administration planned to build a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than bringing them back to the United States. A Kenyan court blocked the government from permitting the facility to proceed.

Some experts have criticized the White House approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could harm treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Rep. Frederica Wilson to retire after 16 years in Congress
cards.teaser: The 83-year-old Florida Democrat confirmed she will not seek reelection in November, becoming the 30th House Democrat from the current Congress who will not join the next.
cards.body:
Rep. Frederica Wilson confirmed she will retire from Congress after serving 16 years in the House. The Miami Herald reported the announcement, which Wilson is expected to make formally at an event in her South Florida district.

Wilson had been under pressure not to run for reelection after missing weeks of House votes while recovering from major eye surgery. She initially denied reporting that she would step aside, but reversed course and told multiple elected officials in her district that she would retire. She becomes the 30th House Democrat from the 119th Congress who will not be joining the 120th.

cards.headline: Guatemala president denies agreement on joint drug strikes with US
cards.teaser: President Bernardo Arévalo said there is no agreement for joint anti-drug trafficking strikes with the US military on Guatemalan soil, but confirmed collaboration to intensify the fight against drug trafficking.
cards.body:
Guatemalan President Bernardo Arévalo said his country has requested US military cooperation in its fight against drug trafficking, including access to equipment, training, and expert assistance. He spoke with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to confirm the terms of cooperation.

Arévalo clarified that the arrangement does not include joint US military operations on Guatemalan soil. The cooperation falls within existing bilateral agreements between the two countries.

cards.headline: Chinese curriculum used in US public schools despite Confucius Institute closures
cards.teaser: Students learning Chinese in public schools could be using curriculum shaped by the Chinese Communist Party, even after many Confucius Institutes closed.
cards.body:
Public school students learning Chinese may be using curriculum shaped by the Chinese Communist Party. The influence persists under a new name despite the closure of many Confucius Institutes across the United States in recent years.

Confucius Institutes were Chinese government-funded programs that partnered with American universities and schools to teach Chinese language and culture. Many closed after concerns were raised about foreign influence in US educational institutions.

cards.headline: Speaker Johnson's longtime chief of staff to leave in June
cards.teaser: Hayden Haynes, who has been by Speaker Mike Johnson's side for all of his key achievements since he took the post in 2023, will depart next month.
cards.body:
Hayden Haynes, Speaker Mike Johnson's chief of staff, will depart in June. Haynes has served Johnson since he became Speaker in 2023, supporting him through major legislative initiatives.

The departure marks a significant transition for Johnson's office, as the chief of staff role oversees daily operations, legislative coordination, and strategic planning.

cards.headline: Trump administration shifts homeless policy away from Housing First approach
cards.teaser: The administration is pursuing a different path to address homelessness, focusing on treatment, recovery, and self-sufficiency rather than just providing housing.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is pursuing a different approach to address homelessness, focusing on treatment, recovery, and self-sufficiency rather than just providing housing. The shift moves away from the Housing First model that had been a dominant strategy in recent years.

The administration is prioritizing programs that demonstrate measurable results in treatment, recovery, and self-sufficiency areas. Housing First advocates have long argued that stable housing is a prerequisite for addressing other challenges facing homeless individuals, but critics say the approach has not produced sufficient outcomes.
